name: Root-grown hut
kind: Building shell with a door plate
status: Example. Exterior shell generated, scaled by its door, cleaned, and given a door plate, as a standard 3D model. No interior, not yet in Skyrim's model format and not in the game.
summary: A one-room dwelling of the interior, trained from living root and limb. It shows the buildings route for an organic shape: one generated shell, door included, with the door then found on the real geometry and covered by a plate that would carry the prompt.

need.why: Root pieces are held (ramps, roots, Hist trunks) but no root-grown hut was found in any mod we hold, by name or by looking. The Root-Folk's 19 places have 3 source interiors between them for 22 households.
need.lore: "The interior does not build a house, it trains one. Root and canopy limb are grafted, bent and tied over years into wall, floor, stair and threshold while still alive"; sealed with Hist-sap resin, roofed in bark shingle and layered canopy leaf, never reed thatch, no stone (story/lore/topics/material-culture.md, the grown-root kit).
need.use: Swapped in for a source building at the adapting stage of a Root-Folk place draft, its door on the source door's position, with an interior behind it.

brief.text: A rounded, slightly lopsided dome of thick grafted roots, gaps sealed with amber sap, a roof of bark shingle and broad leaves, one low arched plank door, two round sap windows. No stone, thatch, stilts, metal, ropes, hanging things or thin root tendrils.

fees.note: Fal's list prices for the options used, read on 24 November 2026 from each model's Fal page; Fal's request history shows no charge per request, so these are not from a bill.

stages.name: 1. Reference images
stages.did: Two images from one brief, three-quarter view from the front. Both came back as painted concept art with thin root tendrils spreading over a patch of ground. The better one was then edited into a photograph of the same building with the tendrils and ground removed.
stages.looked: Both read at once as a root-grown hut and match the lore: grafted roots, sap windows, bark and leaf roof, no stone. The first shows its plank door clearly; the second half hides it. As paintings they would bake a painted look into the model, and the tendrils are the canoe's rope again.
stages.decision: Reference 1, edited. Lesson for the brief: ask for a photograph of a physical object by name, and for a flat clean base.
images: Reference 1 as a photograph, tendrils and ground removed: the image the model was made from

stages.name: 2. Generation
stages.verdict: pass at the first try: H3.1 kept
stages.did: The edited image to Tripo H3.1 and Tripo P2, each asked for at most 40,000 triangles.
stages.looked: Both are the hut, from every side: the generator invented a believable back with more roots and sap windows. H3.1 is closed underneath. P2 came back as a hollow shell open at the base, in 226 pieces, with a glossier, wetter look.
stages.decision: H3.1 kept: nearly one closed piece (4 open edges against 7,223).
images: Tripo P2: hollow and in pieces

stages.name: 3. Shaping and clean-up
stages.did: Two loose pieces removed and the triangles cut from 39,104 to 14,000 with the texture layout kept (building.py shell). The size comes from the door, marked by hand in the next step.
stages.looked: The cut does not show from the six views.
stages.decision: Kept. One texture over a building this size gives about 245 pixels per metre, soft at arm's length: walk up to the wall in the viewer and judge it.

stages.name: 4. The door, marked by hand
stages.did: The shell was drawn from its four sides as flat pictures with a grid (building.py view). The door was found by eye on the front and its outline marked as seven points along the painted planks and arch. The tool then scaled the shell so the marked door is 2.3 m high, cast one ray per point inside the outline onto the real surface, fitted the door leaf's own lean, and laid the plate on it, in front of the leaf's proudest part, with the arrival point 1.3 m out. A section through the door from the side checks it.
stages.looked: From the front the outline follows the planks and the arch. From the side the plate leans with the door and stands just clear of the cross-bar; the only part in front of it is a root of the frame at one edge, about 0.5% of the outline's area.
stages.decision: Kept. The automatic door finder is gone: a door is always marked by eye. The door is narrower than a vanilla house door (1.4 m against 1.4 to 1.8).
images: The four sides as drawn for marking: the door is on the first
The marked door from the front, and the section from the side: grey is the surface, orange the plate

stages.name: 5. Interior and the game
stages.decision: Still owed: a matching interior of one or more rooms; collision a player can walk against; a distant-view model; repeating bark, sap and shingle materials so the wall is sharp up close; Skyrim's model format; one swap into a Root-Folk place draft; your look in game.

stages.name: Cost experiment: cheaper generators
stages.did: The same reference image went once to each cheaper route on Fal, and to Meshy 7.1. Every result is scaled to the brief (tobrief.py) before it is shown, so all of them stand in true metres beside the 1.8 m person.

measured.prices: Prices are Fal's list prices, not from a bill.
measured.seconds: The generator's own reported time where it reports one; Trellis 2, Hunyuan and Tripo do not report it.

stages.looked: Each result was looked at from six fixed views; the one-line note per route is in the table.
stages.decision: The owner's pick is Tripo H3.1: the best shape and the best texture of all three things. The rest are listed under 'Other generators tried', ranked.

Idol max turbo, $0.10: kept after clean-up

routes.look: Clearly the root hut: arched plank door, glowing amber windows, roots and leaf roof. 13 small loose pieces and 17 open edges; the roof leaves are pale and blotchy.
Looks right from outside, but the shell is full of holes (7,092 open edges) and 212 loose pieces, and the underside shows camouflage-like smears.
Reads as the hut, with door and amber windows; the roof is a smooth tan with little detail, it stands taller than the others, and 19 stray bits float under it.
Rejected before it ran: the reference image was 2,083 KB and this route takes at most 950 KB. Nothing came back.
The richest of the set: layered leaf roof, door, lit windows that show through inside; but 248 small loose pieces to remove (the building tool already does this).
A rich hut with a good door, but more windows than the brief and 384 loose pieces to clear. Three times H3.1's price.
